products.title: Cadefihuila
products.body_html:
Origin: Nieva, Huila

Cooperative: Cadefihuila

Processing: Washed

Varietal(s): Caturra, Castillo

Altitude: 1,100 - 1,550 MASL

Roast Level: Medium

Cupping Notes: Red Apple, Green Grape, Molasses

Certifications: Rainforest Alliance

Discover the vibrant character of our Single Origin Colombian Coffee Beans from Nieva, Huila—one of Colombia’s most celebrated coffee regions. Sourced from the Cadefihuila Cooperative, these Rainforest Alliance certified beans are cultivated on small farms at high altitudes (1,100–1,550 MASL), allowing the unique terroir of the Andes to shine through in every cup.

Expertly washed and medium roasted, this lot—featuring Caturra and Castillo varietals—delivers an exceptionally clean and balanced profile. Enjoy notes of red apple, green grape, and molasses in a cup that’s as refreshing as it is complex.

Cadefihuila has empowered generations of farmers since 1963, promoting sustainable practices and quality at every stage. When you choose our single origin Colombian coffee beans, you’re not just getting world-class flavor—you’re supporting a legacy of community and environmental stewardship.

Perfect for coffee lovers seeking authentic, specialty-grade Colombian coffee. Available fresh roasted and shipped directly to your door.

products.title: El Indio
products.body_html:
El Indio Natural
Planadas, Tolima, Colombia — Natural Process

Some coffees show their work. El Indio is one of them.

Every cherry was hand-picked at peak ripeness, then hand-sorted again to remove anything that didn't meet the standard. From there it was sundried on raised beds under temperature-controlled conditions — slow, deliberate, exactly the kind of natural process that rewards patience instead of rushing it.

The result is vibrant and layered — cranberry and dark chocolate up front, honeybell citrus underneath, the kind of brightness that careful natural processing does best. A velvety body holds it all together. Nothing about it asks you to wait for it to open up. It's there from the first sip.

This is 100% Caturra — a variety with roots in Minas Gerais, Brazil, prized for its quality in the cup as much as its resilience in the field. Grown at altitude in Planadas, Tolima, it's the kind of coffee that makes the case for why natural process, done right, is worth seeking out.
Origin Planadas, Tolima, Colombia
Varieties Caturra
Process Natural
Altitude 1,500–2,150 MASL
Roast Medium - Light
Tasting notes Cranberry, Dark Chocolate, Honeybell
Best brewed as Pour over, espresso

 

Best brewed as a pour-over to let the fruit-forward notes come through clearly.

products.title: La Leona
products.body_html:
Luz Helena Salazar — Pink Bourbon Washed
La Leona Farm, Armenia, Quindío, Colombia — Washed Process

Some coffees come with a name worth knowing. This one comes with two.

Luz Helena Salazar has been farming the volcanic soils of Armenia, Quindío for over twenty years — building her craft quietly, improving her practices season by season, and raising two sons who went on to found Cofinet, the export company that brought this coffee to us. The La Leona farm is the result of that work: meticulous, specific, and built on a standard that doesn't cut corners.

The coffee itself is Pink Bourbon — a variety that sounds like it belongs on a cocktail menu but has roots far older than its name suggests. Recent genetic testing identified it as an Ethiopian landrace, which explains something about the cup: there's a brightness to it, a clarity, that reads more like East Africa than South America. Key lime and raspberry up front, caramel underneath to hold it all together. It's a light roast, and it shows — clean, layered, and worth slowing down for.

The process is careful by design. Cherries are harvested following strict ripeness criteria, floated and hand-sorted to remove any defects, then exposed to 30 hours of underwater fermentation before being pulped. The parchment is gently washed and dried under temperature-controlled conditions until ideal moisture is reached. Nothing rushed. Nothing left to chance.

This is the kind of coffee that rewards attention. Luz Helena spent twenty years earning the right to grow it that way.

Producer Luz Helena Salazar
Farm La Leona
Origin Armenia, Quindío, Colombia
Process Washed — 30hr underwater fermentation
Altitude 1,450-1,500 MASL
Variety Pink Bourbon
Roast Light
Tasting notes Key Lime, Raspberry, Caramel
Best brewed as Pour-over

products.title: Galeras
products.body_html:
Origin: Galeras, Narino, Colombia

Processing: Washed

Altitude: 1,600-2,100 MASL

Roast Level: Dark Medium

Cupping Notes: Vanilla, Smoked Toffee, Dark Chocolate

High in the mountains of Nariño, Colombia, coffee thrives in the shadow of the Galeras Volcano. With elevations reaching 2,100 meters and rich volcanic soil, the cherries here mature slowly, developing concentrated sugars and complexity that make this region’s coffees some of the most admired in Colombia.

This washed lot comes from smallholder farmers—many cultivating just a single hectare—who carefully harvest ripe cherries before a 20–25 hour fermentation. Drying is done in parabolic dryers with controlled airflow and temperature to protect quality and create consistency. The result is a coffee that highlights both the terroir and the dedication of its producers.

Roasted to a dark medium, this coffee reveals a bolder side of Nariño: layers of toffee and vanilla pair with the region’s signature dark chocolate and black fruit depth. The cup is sweet, rounded, and comforting, with enough structure to shine whether brewed as a filter or pulled as a rich espresso.

products.title: Tirra F1 (Natural)
products.body_html:
Tirra F1 — Natural
San Marcos de Tarrazú, Costa Rica — Natural Process

CoopeTarrazú has been farming the Los Santos Zone since 1960 — nearly 5,000 families working volcanic soil at elevation in one of the most respected coffee regions in Costa Rica. They don't cut corners. They don't chase trends. And on their own experimental farm, they've been quietly doing something most cooperatives don't attempt: breeding the next generation of coffee.

F1 refers to the first-generation offspring of two deliberately selected parent varieties bred to capture what neither parent alone reliably produces. In Costa Rica, this work has been developed through programs involving CATIE, CIRAD, and PROMECAFE, combining high-quality Arabica genetics with disease-resistant lines to produce varieties that are more resilient at the farm level and more expressive in the cup. The best F1 lots have competed at the highest levels of specialty coffee. This is that category.

What CoopeTarrazú's experimental farm produced this season is exactly what F1 development promises when it's done right. Naturally processed, light roasted, and unlike anything we've carried from Tarrazú before.

Strawberry and mango up front. A fruit sherbet quality that hits the palate with a sparkling effervescence on the finish. Brewed as a pour-over it opens into something layered and vivid that keeps changing as it cools: clean, bright, and completely unlike what most people expect when they hear Costa Rica.

We were glad to secure some of this. We're also being straightforward: this is a limited experimental lot from a farm that isn't producing at scale. There is no reorder this season. When it's gone, it's gone.

Producer CoopeTarrazú
Farm Experimental Farm, San Marcos de Tarrazú
Origin Tarrazú, Costa Rica
Process Natural
Variety F1 Hybrid
Roast Light
Tasting notes Strawberry, Mango, Fruit Sherbet
Best brewed as Pour-over

products.title: Pastora
products.body_html:
Origin: Tarrazu, Costa Rica

Processing: Washed

Altitude: 1,450-1,500 MASL

Varieties: Caturra & Catuai

Roast Level: Light-Medium

Cupping Notes: Raisin, Dark Chocolate, Black Tea, Honey, Fuji Apple

La Pastora stands out as the benchmark for Costa Rica single origin coffee beans.

Grown in the renowned San Jose province and processed by the respected CoopeTarrazú cooperative, this washed coffee is approachable, clean, and classic, with a juicy twist. Balanced notes of syrupy plum and subtle nuttiness make La Pastora the perfect choice for any brew method.

What makes these Costa Rica single origin coffee beans unique is the rich, sedimentary mountain soil of San Jose. This exceptional terroir delivers uniform flavor and a vibrant acidity in every cup. CoopeTarrazú, a cooperative representing over 3,500 local coffee growers, is dedicated to sustainable practices and the wellbeing of their farming community.

Choose La Pastora for a coffee experience that captures the essence of Costa Rica—complex fruit character, balanced sweetness, and the classic clarity only true Costa Rica single origin coffee beans can deliver.

products.title: Mapache
products.body_html:
Farm(s): Finca El Naranjito, Finca Casa de Zinc

Origin: Concepcion de Ataco, Ahuachapan

Processing: Washed

Altitude: 1,300 MASL

Roast Level: Dark

Cupping Notes: Cinnamon Spice, Dark Caramel, Tart, Syrupy

Mapache Coffee is a fifth-generation company of coffee producers, owned and managed by Jan-Carlo and Sofia Handtke in the Apaneca Ilamatepec mountain range of El Salvador. Mapache Coffee employs over 125 locals year-round, but during harvest season, their staff swells to 600 people who work together to build coffee nurseries, replant at Mapache’s six farm properties, and process the perfectly ripe cherries that come from them.

Mapache maintains a strong commitment to the well-being of the coffee forests, ensuring that every farm has a canopy protecting the coffee plants and soil. Their modern wet mill uses limited amounts of water during the washing process, then recycles and reuses that water in the same process. All the remaining pulp from the wet milling process is incorporated back into the farms as compost, returning key nutrients to the soil.

Mapache’s Strictly High Grown coffees come from the two Finca El Naranjito properties and Finca Casa de Zinc, three of the company’s six estates. These neighboring farms are located in Concepción de Ataco in the municipality of Ahuachapán. Bourbon and Pacas varieties make up the majority of the crops here, with these three properties accounting for 60 percent of Mapache’s total coffee growing area.

Gifted with an ideal climate for growing coffee, Finca El Naranjito and Casa de Zinc sit at an average of 1,300 meters above sea level with a stellar view of the Pacific Ocean. El Imposible National Park, the largest forest reserve in El Salvador, sits just one mile away. As with all single origin El Salvador coffee beans we source through Mapache, you can be sure that thoughtful preparation and consistency shine through in the cup.

products.title: Ixlama
products.body_html:
Origin: Huehuetenango

Processing: Washed

Altitude: 1,520 - 1,830 MASL

Roast Level: Medium

Cupping Notes: Strawberry, Brown Sugar, Clean & Balanced

It's BACK! 

Last season this coffee was a customer favorite (and Michele's) and we are so happy we held out for it again. 

We sampled so many single origin Guatemalan coffee beans in anticipation of what this origin can offer. There were a few that could stand on their own, but none cupped nearly as strong as Ixlama. Sometimes, you gotta just wait for the good stuff!

This coffee can bring a smile to every coffee lover; throw any brewing method at it - she'll stand on her own. From pour-over to auto drip, this is a coffee that everyone can appreciate no matter the tools in your brewing arsenal.

A true crowd pleaser with a ripened strawberry entrance, a little spice, then a whole lot of sweetness that's delivered in a medium body delight - all with an amazingly clean finish. 

About the coffee...

Huehuetenango Ixlama comes from specialty selected small producers, like Finca El Paternal & Finca Nueva Palmira, from the highlands of San Pedro Necta and La Libertad, both located in the state of Huehuetenango, Guatemala.  This shade grown coffee is harvested and brought to the mill where it is sun-dried on a patio and placed in “guardiolas”.  It is separated by color via computer and density/size mechanically which results in a superior cup.

products.title: Finca Idealista (Honey)
products.body_html:
Finca Idealista - Black Honey
Matagalpa, Nicaragua — Black Honey Process

Ben Weiner didn't come to coffee the usual way.

He came to Nicaragua first — through a senior thesis on debt relief, through trips into the mountains outside Matagalpa, through a growing conviction that the best way to change something is to be present in it. Gold Mountain Coffee Growers grew out of that work, connecting smallholder Nicaraguan farmers to specialty roasters worldwide. Finca Idealista is Ben's own farm — the flagship of everything Gold Mountain has built — and it operates the way you'd expect from someone who chose this place on principle.

Machetes instead of herbicides. A mushroom to kill insects instead of pesticides. Volcanic filters to keep mucilage-filled wash-water out of the watershed. Chickens roosting above the compost to infuse it with nitrogen. Pickers paid double local rates. And one more detail that says everything about where Ben's priorities sit: Finca Idealista bought a rainforest just to protect it.

The coffee reflects all of it.

This is a black honey microlot — Pacas and Caturra grown at 1,200 meters in Matagalpa, processed at the maximum mucilage level possible and dried slowly in the sun. The result is full-bodied, sweet, and layered in a way that changes as it cools. Candied citrus and honey up front, rooibos tea and a smooth brown sugar finish as the cup opens up. Slightly earthy. Incredibly complex. The kind of coffee that rewards a slow pour-over on a morning when you're not in a hurry.

Producer Benjamin Weiner - Gold Mountain Coffee Growers
Farm Finca Idealista
Origin Matagalpa, Nicaragua
Process Black Honey
Altitude 1,200 MASL
Variety Pacas & Caturra
Roast Light
Tasting notes Candied Citrus, Honey, Rooibos Tea
Best brewed as Pour-over

products.title: Vecindad
products.body_html:
Farmer: Member Farmers of Gold Mountain Coffee Growers

Farm: Various

Location at Origin: Mataglapa, Jinotega

Processing: Natural 

Altitude: 1,300 to 1,600 MASL

Varieties: Catuai, Caturra, Bourbon, Pache Colis, Geisha

Roast Level: Light

Cupping Notes: Dried Pineapple, Sugar, Wildflower Honey

The Story

Vecindad is a coffee built through collaboration. Sourced through our partners at Gold Mountain Coffee Growers, this lot brings together coffees from neighboring producers across the Matagalpa and Jinotego regions of Nicaragua.

Each of these farms produces a small amount of natural-processed coffee — not enough on its own to form a single exportable lot. Rather than letting those coffees go unnoticed, they’re carefully combined, creating a profile that reflects the shared work and collective effort of the community.

It’s a thoughtful approach that allows smaller producers to participate in the specialty market while producing something truly distinctive in the cup.rom the fruit to concentrate into the seed, building both sweetness and body.

The Process

Each contributing farm harvests ripe coffee cherry and processes it as a natural, drying the fruit intact on raised beds. This slow drying allows sugars from the fruit to concentrate into the seed, building both sweetness and body.

Once dried and prepared, the coffees are blended at origin with intention — preserving quality while creating a balanced, expressive final lot.

In the Cup

Vecindad is fruit-forward and inviting, with a profile that feels both vibrant and composed.

Expect pineapple up front — bright, tropical, and lively — followed by a soft, rounded sweetness of raw sugar and honey. The cup carries a full, silky body, offering depth without heaviness and a finish that lingers just long enough to bring you back for another sip.

It’s a coffee that feels layered without being overwhelming — it's both approachable and drinkable, but still interesting.

Why We Love It

This is the kind of coffee that reminds us how much potential exists in thoughtful sourcing. By bringing together smaller lots with care, Vecindad delivers a profile that’s both dynamic and easy to enjoy.

It’s equally at home as a daily drinker or something you slow down with — a balance we’re always looking for. 

Vecindad is a reflection of shared work at origin - and a reminder that great coffee doesn't always come from a single place but from people working collectively for something beautiful together. 

Gold Mountain Coffee Growers is a social enterprise that, in addition to its own farm (Finca Idealista), works directly with coffee producers in Nicaragua, including Guadalupe, to connect them with roasters abroad. GMCG is on the ground, all the time, teaming up with producers willing to take the steps necessary (and whose altitude and soil conditions allow them) to produce high-cupping specialty coffee. We literally stand on every partner farm during picking to ensure ripeness with refractometers and ripeness bracelets. GMCG also carries out sustainable development projects in communities, such as free computing classes for girls from coffee communities, medical assistance, microcredit, running water in schools, and educational supplies.

products.title: Drift
products.body_html:
Permission to pause. Space to savor.

Steel Oak Coffee’s Drift Blend is a specialty coffee created in collaboration with our friends at Yes Coffee in Flagler Beach. Built on a foundation of Brazilian, Colombian, and Guatemalan coffees, Drift was designed to deliver comfort in the cup and versatility across brew methods.

This medium roast blend leans into its confectionary side—layered with milk chocolate, caramel, and nougat that make it taste like your favorite candy bar in coffee form. Smooth and balanced as a filter brew, bold and decadent as an espresso, Drift is equally at home sipped black or paired with milk and syrups.

But Drift is more than flavor—it’s a feeling. It’s the permission to slow down, to let your mind wander, and to enjoy a cup without hurry. Every sip is crafted to give you that moment of ease, whether you’re brewing at home, sharing with friends, or pulling shots behind the bar.

products.title: Summer Swell 2026

Summer Swell Colombia · Costa Rica · Nicaragua — Washed

This year's version is three washed coffees from Colombia, Costa Rica, and Nicaragua - together they landed exactly where we wanted: black tea, brown sugar, and Florida lemon. Clean and bright the way a good summer morning is supposed to be.

No dark roast drama.

No complexity that demands your full attention.

Just a coffee that's easy to love and hard to put down — whether it's a cup on the porch at 7am or a cold brew in a glass by noon.

Summer Swell comes back every year when summer in Ormond Beach arrives. The blend changes to complement the feeling that doesn't.

Tasting notes Black tea, brown sugar, Florida lemon
Best brewed as Drip, cold brew

Discover why Thrive Blend is quickly becoming a customer favorite—order yours today and taste specialty coffee at its best.

products.title: James Hoffmann Fermentation Project Tasting Kit
products.body_html:
James Hoffmann Fermentation Project — Tasting Kit
Steel Oak Coffee × James Hoffmann × Lucia Solis

Some coffees tell you about a place. This one tells you about a process.

The James Hoffmann Fermentation Project is a global cupping event created by James Hoffmann and fermentation scientist Lucia Solis, distributed through a select group of specialty roasters worldwide.

Every kit contains four coffees from the same single harvest at Finca San Miguel Urias in the Antigua Valley, Guatemala (grown by Hector and Lilian Leal of Rueda Farms).

What changes across the four bags is the only variable Hoffmann and Solis wanted you to taste: what happens to the seed during fermentation, before it dries.

Same farm. Same harvest. Same roastery. The only variable is the fermentation method, and that single variable produces four meaningfully different coffees.

We roast all four lots with the same intention, let the fermentation speak. Whatever you taste that differs between these cups belongs to the processing.

On October 3, 2026, James Hoffmann hosts the global live tasting on his YouTube channel.

Thousands of people around the world, same four coffees, same moment. Taste from home with your kit, or come find us in Ormond Beach. We'll be pouring all four.

What's in the kit? Each kit contains four 80g bags.

Bag #1: 80g Mechanically Demucilaged (Control)
Mucilage removed by machine with no biological fermentation. The baseline, the coffee's terroir, variety, and growing conditions with nothing added.

Bag #2: 80g Wild Fermentation
A traditional 48-hour submerged fermentation using naturally occurring local microorganisms from the farm environment. The process generations of producers have relied on.

Bag #3: 80g Lactobacillus Inoculated
A 48-hour submerged fermentation inoculated with Lactobacillus bacteria. Promotes the production of organic acids — typically lifting brightness, vibrancy, and aromatic complexity.

Bag #4: 80g Saccharomyces Yeast Inoculated
A 48-hour submerged fermentation inoculated with Saccharomyces yeast. Promotes flavor precursor development — typically enhancing body, texture, and the perception of sweetness.


Farm Finca San Miguel Urias, Antigua Valley, Guatemala
Producer Hector and Lilian Leal, Rueda Farms
Fermentation Protocols Designed by Lucia Solis
Altitude 1,460–1,540 masl
Variety Caturra, H1, Bourbon
Format 4 × 80g (320g total), whole bean only
 

A Note on Timing

The coffees supporting this kit are planned to be roasted on September 7th; a single roast date, by design. James Hoffmann's team asked all participating roasters to align on timing so that every kit shipped worldwide is working from the same rest window before the October 3rd event.

Orders must be placed by Sunday, September 13th. All kits will be shipped on Monday, September 14th.

After that date, any remaining kits will be available for purchase in person at the roastery, while supplies last. When they're gone, they're gone.
